name: Wine-grower record books and declarations desk
buyer: Small and family wineries and grape growers (several thousand, mostly South Moravia); no verified count
trigger: Evidence books (Act 321/2004 Sb., vyhl. 323/2004 Sb.) must be written up by the next working day after grape intake (per NSS ruling citing Reg. 436/2009, which may have been replaced; check). Annual declarations to ÚKZÚZ: harvest by 15 Jan, production if 1,000 l or more, stocks (stocks date in the 2025 calendar was 10 Sept), plus a quarterly or annual vineyard-area report for the Wine Fund. SZPI checks the books and fines errors.
evidence: MZe 2025 calendar for vine growers and winemakers; portal.gov.cz service S19407; NSS ruling on the deadline for entering records (sbirka.nssoud.cz p2882). Filing runs through the free Portál farmáře, but the books themselves are kept by the winery. Czech law may not allow electronic books; this was not confirmed.
existing: Competitor searches (two, Czech) found only foreign winery tools (Vinosoft, VinBalance, InnoVint, EVINAR) and no Czech winery software or Excel template. Not verified that none exists.
unchecked: Whether Czech rules allow electronic evidence books; Czech vendors; current Reg. 436/2009 replacement; number of winemakers; SZPI fine levels; 2026 dates.

first_check.duty: Act 321/2004 Sb. and decree 88/2017 Sb. § 13 (amended by 305/2023 Sb.), which replaced 323/2004 Sb. (the transition ended 31 Jul 2017). Evidence books follow Annexes 12-26: grape harvest and intake, purchase slips, processing and output by quality class, sucrose and enrichment, monthly wine stocks, and per-vessel stock and treatment cards. Producers under 500 hl a year may use the combined Annex 23/24. The decree explicitly allows electronic books if software makes each entry irreversible and records who made it, so the claim's doubt on this point is resolved. Deadlines for most books follow the directly applicable EU rules. Reg. 436/2009 has been replaced, I believe by Delegated Reg. 2018/273 and Implementing Reg. 2018/274, but I did not confirm this in the session. For bulk wine, entries are due by the next working day and monthly stocks by the 3rd working day. Declarations: harvest by 15 Jan (only growers who sell grapes or must), production and stocks (2025 calendar: stocks as of 31 Jul due by 10 Sep), and Wine Fund levy reports. These go through the free eAgri/Portál farmáře Registr vinic or the SZPI portal. SZPI supervises, and the NSS ruling upholds fines for incomplete records. I did not check fine amounts or the 2026 dates.
first_check.market: 2,236 registered wine producers under § 11 of Act 321/2004, plus 596 bulk-wine sellers under § 16b (MZe information-request response, 2021). 13,732 growers with planted vineyards at 31 Dec 2022 (Česká spořitelna, using ÚKZÚZ data), and 16,541 growers in the ČSÚ Vinice 2020 survey. Most are very small, many of them hobby growers.
first_check.competitor: Free state filing channels already exist: the eAgri/Portál farmáře Registr vinic (built by CCV Informační systémy) and the SZPI portal for declarations and wine classification. They cover filing only, not the cellar books. In six Czech and English searches I found no Czech winery evidence-book software, only foreign tools (vintrace, InnoVint, Vintners Advantage, Vinsight, and the Slovenian EVINAR). It is possible that Czech ERP add-ons or small local vendors exist and are poorly indexed. That remains unverified.
first_check.reason: The duty is real and in force. Act 321/2004 Sb. and its implementing decree 88/2017 Sb. (amended by 305/2023; it replaced 323/2004) require evidence books in Annexes 12-26: intake, processing, monthly stocks, per-vessel cards, and a simplified Annex 23/24 for producers under 500 hl. The decree explicitly allows electronic books if every entry is irreversible and names who made it. Wineries also file harvest, production and stock declarations through free eAgri/Portál farmáře and SZPI portals, and NSS case law upholds fines for late or incomplete entries. In six Czech searches I found no Czech vendor, only foreign tools. A niche of about 2,200 registered producers, many of them hobby-sized, limits willingness to pay. A low-cost subscription that prints the books and pre-fills the declarations is plausible.

challenge_check.killer: None found. FULLCOM FIS may have a vineyard-records extension, but this rests only on a VŠB thesis abstract and was not verified.
challenge_check.reason: I found nothing that kills this. Eight Czech and English searches turned up no Czech product for keeping the cellar books. The only Czech lead is a VŠB bachelor's thesis that extends FULLCOM's FIS ERP with vineyard records, and it is not confirmed as a product. The state's free tools only handle filing. The market is small: 2,236 registered wine producers (MZe, around 2020-21, undated) and about 13,700 growers, mostly hobby-scale and short of money. Two legal references in the claim are out of date: decree 323/2004 has been replaced by 88/2017 Sb., and EU Reg. 436/2009 by Reg. 2018/273 and 2018/274. Still unconfirmed: whether Czech law allows electronic books, and whether small local vendors that search engines index poorly exist.
